title: Uruk expansion (Late Uruk interaction sphere)
summary: During the Middle and Late Uruk periods, about 3700–3100 BCE, southern Mesopotamians reached neighbouring Iran, Syria and Anatolia. Uruk itself grew to roughly 2.5 square km. At Hacinebi in Turkey a small Mesopotamian colony lived beside local people for at least two centuries.

uncertainty.note: Stein dates the Middle and Late Uruk expansion to ca. 3700–3100 B.C.; Woods gives the Late Uruk period as ca. 3350–3100 bc. The record id uses the conventional c. 3200 BCE for the later phase.

as_recorded.value: Middle and Late Uruk periods (ca. 3700–3100 B.C.)

where.modern_name: Uruk (Warka), Iraq, source region; contact zones in Iran, Syria and Turkey
where.historical_name: Uruk (Unug) and southern Mesopotamia, with the Zagros, north Syria and southeast Anatolia

importance.justification: The earliest well-documented case of one urban society projecting settlements and material culture over a wide area.

sources.title: Indigenous Social Complexity at Hacinebi (Turkey) and the Organization of Uruk Colonial Contact (chapter 8)
sources.author: Gil J. Stein

sources.title: The Earliest Mesopotamian Writing, in Visible Language (OIMP 32)
sources.publisher: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures (formerly Oriental Institute), University of Chicago

reviewer_note: The "colonies" reading is debated (Stein stresses symmetric exchange). The pin is Uruk with 1000 km uncertainty; the regional spread is stated, not mapped. Godin Tepe was not confirmed on a page I opened.
